newsitem.title: USA: CME live cattle drop late, end at day's lows.
newsitem.headline: CME live cattle drop late, end at day's lows.

text.p: Higher fed cattle prices failed to materialize and CME live cattle futures dropped for net losses and finished at or near day's lows. Feeder cattle gains also were pared by spillover pressure, traders said.
Live cattle ended 0.350 to 0.125 cent a lb lower with December off 0.225 at 66.925 cents. February was off most at 63.975.

Longs liquidated positions when cash cattle continued to trade at $68 per cwt instead of rising to $69 as expected. Pressure increased when boxed beef values were quoted lower at noon, adding to speculation that packers will likely obtain needed slaughter numbers at lower prices, traders said.

Early strength came on expectations packers would raise bids for fed cattle as contract cattle appeared too "green" and needed more days on feed. But lower beef prices turned ideas to weaker cash markets, especially since packers would not budge from their $68 bids, they said.

The short time period between Thanksgiving and Christmas appears to be weighing on beef prices. There is normally more time between the two for retailers to feature beef but this year there are fewer weekends before traditional holiday meats such as hams or turkeys dominate display cases, they added.
